sections.heading: C — Communicating intentions and adjusting speed
sections.markdown:
## C — Communicating intentions and adjusting speed

FACT_ID: sec14-F01 | anchor: A01
Let other road users know both your presence and your intended action so they are not surprised. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0120]

FACT_ID: sec14-F02 | anchor: A01
Headlights help other drivers detect your vehicle in rain, snow and fog. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0120]

FACT_ID: sec14-F03 | anchor: A01
When the windshield wipers are turned on, the headlights must also be on. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0120]

FACT_ID: sec14-F04 | anchor: A01
Switch on headlights as darkness begins so others can see the vehicle. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0120]

FACT_ID: sec14-F05 | anchor: A01
Use headlights when driving requires lights; parking lamps serve parked vehicles. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0120]

FACT_ID: sec14-F06 | anchor: A01
When traveling away from a low rising or setting sun, use headlights to help opposing drivers see you. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0120]

FACT_ID: sec14-F07 | anchor: A01
A horn can attract another road user’s attention to help prevent a collision. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0120]

FACT_ID: sec14-F08 | anchor: A01
A light horn tap can alert a driver beginning to move into your lane or failing to notice you. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0120]

FACT_ID: sec14-F09 | anchor: A01
Use a sharp horn warning when a child or older person is about to enter the street, another vehicle may strike you, or your out-of-control vehicle is moving toward a person [A01].
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0120]

FACT_ID: sec14-F10 | anchor: A01
Do not use the horn to hurry another driver, criticize a mistake or greet a friend. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0120]

FACT_ID: sec14-F11 | anchor: A01
Do not sound the horn around a blind pedestrian. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0120]

FACT_ID: sec14-F12 | anchor: A02
If a vehicle breaks down on a highway, make it visible to other drivers. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0121]

FACT_ID: sec14-F13 | anchor: A02
When available, use a telephone or two-way radio to notify authorities of a breakdown and consult posted emergency contact information. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0121]

FACT_ID: sec14-F14 | anchor: A02
If vehicle trouble forces a stop, get off the roadway away from traffic if possible and activate hazard flashers. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0121]

FACT_ID: sec14-F15 | anchor: A02
If you cannot leave the roadway, stop where others can see the vehicle clearly, rather than immediately beyond a hill or curve. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0121]

FACT_ID: sec14-F16 | anchor: A02
Emergency warning devices behind a disabled vehicle give approaching drivers notice and room to change lanes. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0121]

FACT_ID: sec14-F17 | anchor: A02
Without warning devices, the handbook describes warning traffic from a safe roadside position, using a white cloth if available. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0121]

FACT_ID: sec14-F18 | anchor: A02
Never stand in a traffic lane or change a tire if that requires occupying the lane. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0121]

FACT_ID: sec14-F19 | anchor: A02
A raised hood or a white cloth tied to an antenna, mirror or door handle can signal an emergency. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0121]

FACT_ID: sec14-F20 | anchor: A02
Avoid driving beside and slightly behind another vehicle, where its driver may not see you. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0121]

FACT_ID: sec14-F21 | anchor: A02
When passing, clear the other driver’s blind spot promptly rather than lingering there. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0121]

FACT_ID: sec14-F22 | anchor: A02
Do not remain alongside a bus or truck because large vehicles have extensive blind areas. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0121]

FACT_ID: sec14-F23 | anchor: A03
Warn following drivers before changing direction or slowing so they have time to respond. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0122]

FACT_ID: sec14-F24 | anchor: A03
Signal before turning, changing lanes, merging or parking, even when no other road user is visible. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0122]

FACT_ID: sec14-F25 | anchor: A03
The handbook recommends signaling at least three seconds before a maneuver while separately stating the 300-foot legal requirement before a turn. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0122]

FACT_ID: sec14-F26 | anchor: A03
Signaling before an intervening entrance or waiting vehicle can mislead another driver about where you intend to turn. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0122]

FACT_ID: sec14-F27 | anchor: A03
After a turn or lane change, check that the signal has canceled and switch it off manually if necessary. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0122]

FACT_ID: sec14-F28 | anchor: A03
When slowing somewhere unexpected, the handbook recommends tapping the brake pedal three or four times to alert following drivers. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0122]

FACT_ID: sec14-F29 | anchor: A03
Warn when slowing to turn from a road without an exit lane, to park near an intersection, or for an obstruction hidden from following traffic. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0122]

FACT_ID: sec14-F30 | anchor: A03
Give a hand-and-arm signal, an electrical turn signal, or both continuously for at least 300 feet before turning. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0122]

FACT_ID: sec14-F31 | anchor: A03
At higher speeds, the handbook recommends signaling over a longer distance, particularly for expressway lane changes. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0122]

Misconceptions: Preserve the source’s conditions, exceptions and may-versus-must distinction when recalling a rule.
Mnemonics: Use “cause, condition, consequence” as an authored cue for reviewing each cited rule.
Glossary: The key source terms are retained in the individual facts and their domain labels.
Dynamic facts: Contact details, provider lists and current service availability require fresh confirmation and stay outside the stable fact set.

items.skill: Signal presence, turns and unexpected slowing
items.why: Warning purpose, timing and legally required distance must remain distinct.

items.skill: Adjust to traction and merging conditions
items.why: Surface, visibility and traffic flow change the required speed and space.
